AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=llm_model; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_llm_model_provider_model_name, tableName=llm_model; insert tableName=llm_model; insert tableName=llm_model

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=llm_usage; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=llm_usage, constraintName=fk_llm_usage_llm_model, referencedTableName=llm_model; createIndex indexName=idx_llm_usage_created_at, tableName=llm_usage; createIndex indexName=idx_llm_u...

The table is an addition to the spec's list: Phase 2 has no suggestion row yet, and usage must be recorded even when the call failed or the output was rejected by schema validation. provider and model_name are denormalized so a usage row stays readable after the registry row is renamed, and model_id is nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL so the history survives a registry change.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=app_setting
COMMENTS: Stored settings (spec v2 section 9: the Settings screen drives the registry and the AI switch from the browser). A single key/value table rather than one table per switch, so the ignore paths of the same screen can be added later without another migration. The AI master switch lives here with the deployment property as its default: no row means "follow bcosmos.ai.enabled", a row overrides it.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=file_content; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=file_content, constraintName=fk_file_content_file_record, referencedTableName=file_record
COMMENTS: The text of the analysed revision, one row per file record (spec v2 section 7.2/7.3). Two Phase 3 needs force this: the chunker must read the source of a symbol without touching the repository on disk (the file may have changed since the run), and the PatchValidator must apply a proposed diff to the very revision that was analysed. It is an addition to the spec's table list, deliberately kept out of file_record so a findings page never has to transfer the content of every file it mentions. Deleting BCosmos metadata still never touches the original repository: this is a copy inside BCosmos' own database.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=code_chunk; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=code_chunk, constraintName=fk_code_chunk_analysis_run, referencedTableName=analysis_run; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=code_chunk, constraintName=fk_code_chunk_file_record,...
COMMENTS: One chunk per method or type (spec v2 section 4.1 and 7.2). symbol_id is not nullable and is unique per (run, model) because chunking is by symbol by design: no arbitrary character splits, and re-embedding with the same model replaces a row instead of piling up duplicates. text is stored so a suggestion can cite the exact code that was embedded, and embed_model is stored because a vector is only comparable with vectors of the same model and width (spec 7.2).

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=suggestion; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=suggestion, constraintName=fk_suggestion_finding, referencedTableName=finding; addForeignKeyConstraint baseTableName=suggestion, constraintName=fk_suggestion_llm_model, referencedT...
COMMENTS: One AI answer for one finding (spec v2 sections 4.1 and 7.3). response_json keeps the whole structured answer (summary, explanation, cited evidence, risks, tests, uncertainties) and validation_json the verdict the PatchValidator computed, so a reviewed suggestion can be read back without calling a provider again. status is the review decision, and reviewed_at says when a human made it. responses have to stay readable after a model row is renamed, so model_id is nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: addColumn tableName=llm_model; sql
COMMENTS: Phase 3 embeddings need two facts the registry did not carry: what a model is for, and how wide its vectors are. capability is an addition to the spec's column list (like is_default and updated_at before it): without it, making an embedding model the default would silently break every chat call, and a chat model could be handed to embed(). embedding_dimension records the width the provider was asked for, which the runtime compares with bcosmos.retrieval.embedding-dimension and with the code_chunk.embedding column, so a mismatch is refused with a clear message instead of failing inside Postgres. Existing rows are chat models.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: insert tableName=llm_model; insert tableName=llm_model
COMMENTS: gemini-embedding-2 is Google's current embedding model (gemini-embedding-001 stays available until its announced shutdown, but it is the older one); its default output is 3072 dimensions, so the adapter asks for 1536 via embedContentConfig.outputDimensionality. text-embedding-3-small is natively 1536. A vector is only comparable with vectors from the same model and width, so switching the embedding model is a re-embedding operation, not a settings toggle.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=commit_record; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_commit_record_repository_hash, tableName=commit_record; createIndex indexName=idx_commit_record_repository_committed_at, tableName=commit_record
COMMENTS: One row per commit the miner discovered (spec v2 section 4.1). It is what makes the pipeline's progress answerable from Postgres alone: the corpus status endpoint reads this table instead of asking Kafka or the worker what happened. author_hash stores an already-hashed author identity, never an email or a name, so the corpus carries no personal data (spec section 10). The unique constraint on (repository_id, hash) is the idempotency key of the ingest side: the miner may publish the same commit twice (at-least-once delivery) and the second write is an update, not a duplicate row (spec section 5.3). parent_hashes is a Postgres text array because a merge commit has more than one parent. changed_java_files is a count, not the list: the list travels on the event and would only be re-derived metadata in this table.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: dropNotNullConstraint columnName=canonical_local_path, tableName=repository; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_repository_remote_url, tableName=repository; sql
COMMENTS: A repository the miner clones has no local path of its own: it lives in the miner's own cache, which is private to that process and is not something the backend owns or may invent. Until now canonical_local_path was NOT NULL, which forced a mined repository row to state a path that did not exist. The column becomes nullable, and a check constraint keeps the invariant that actually matters: a LOCAL repository has a canonical path and no remote URL, a MINED repository has a remote URL and no local path.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=worker_file_result; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_worker_file_result_key, tableName=worker_file_result; createIndex indexName=idx_worker_file_result_repo_commit, tableName=worker_file_result
COMMENTS: Idempotency tracking table for the worker (spec v2 section 5.3, ADR 0027). Records each file processed for a given (repository_id, commit_hash, file_path, side, analyzer_version, ruleset_hash). A redelivered message for the exact same tuple is detected here and skipped or updated rather than duplicating findings.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=gold_run; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_gold_run_version_source, tableName=gold_run; createTable tableName=agg_pipeline_stat; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_agg_pipeline_stat_key, tableName=agg_pipeline_stat; create...
COMMENTS: The gold tables of Phase 5 (spec v2 sections 4.1 and 6.1). Spark writes them and the backend only ever reads them: the REST API never talks to Spark (spec section 6.1, `load_gold`). Every table carries dataset_version and generated_at, so a chart can say which snapshot it shows, and a later run replaces the rows of the tables as a whole snapshot while an older dataset_version stays readable until it is pruned. `gold_run` is the snapshot header the Analytics screen shows; `agg_finding` is the drill-down layer, capped by `load_gold` to the most recent commits per repository so Postgres does not become a second copy of the whole event stream.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: createTable tableName=llm_provider; addUniqueConstraint constraintName=uq_llm_provider_code, tableName=llm_provider; insert tableName=llm_provider; insert tableName=llm_provider; insert tableName=llm_provider; insert tableName=llm_provider; insert tabl...
COMMENTS: A provider becomes a row instead of a Java enum value (Phase 11, spec v2 sections 7.1 and 10). Before this change the set of callable providers was fixed at compile time (GEMINI, OPENAI_COMPATIBLE) and each one had exactly one base URL and one API key, both from configuration - so DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama and OpenRouter could not coexist, and Claude needed a new class. Now llm_provider carries the endpoint, the protocol that selects the adapter, and the credential: either an environment variable name, or a key the user pasted, stored encrypted with a master key that itself comes from the environment (ADR 0038). The plaintext key is never a column, is never returned by the API, and api_key_hint holds only the last four characters so the screen can say which key is in place. Existing rows are backfilled by the legacy provider value.

AUTHOR: bcosmos
DESCRIPTION: update tableName=llm_model; update tableName=llm_model
COMMENTS: Two seeded llm_model rows still carry instructions for a configuration path that changeset 0025 removed (bcosmos.ai.providers.openai-compatible.base-url no longer exists: endpoints live on llm_provider rows now). The old changesets are never edited — their checksums are what a deployed database validates against — so the advice is corrected here as data. The WHERE clause matches the seeded wording itself, so a note a user has since rewritten is left alone.
